sections.title: Intuitive Hook: The Area Scaling Factor
sections.content: Introduce the concept of a linear transformation using a 2D square. Explain that a determinant is not just a number, but a 'scaling factor' that tells us how much the area of a shape changes after the transformation.
sections.example: Visualize a unit square being stretched into a parallelogram by a matrix. If the area doubles, the determinant is 2.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The 2x2 Basic Calculation
sections.content: Define the determinant for a 2x2 matrix [[a, b], [c, d]] as ad - bc. Use a graphical overlay showing the cross-multiplication of vectors.
sections.example: Calculate the determinant of matrix A = [[3, 1], [0, 2]]. Result: (3*2) - (1*0) = 6. The area of the resulting shape is 6 times the original.

sections.title: Geometric Signification: Orientation and Zero
sections.content: Explain what a negative determinant means (flipping the orientation, like a mirror image) and what a zero determinant implies (the shape is crushed into a line or point, losing dimension).
sections.example: Imagine a 2D robot arm: if the determinant is 0, the arm is 'locked' and cannot span a 2D plane.

sections.title: Scaling to 3D: Volume Interpretation
sections.content: Extend the concept to 3D. The determinant now represents the volume scaling factor of a parallelepiped. Briefly mention the Laplace expansion for higher dimensions.
sections.example: A 3D cube with side length 1 transformed by a matrix with determinant 0.5; the cube shrinks to half its original volume.

sections.title: Application and Summary
sections.content: Summarize that the determinant is a core tool in solving systems of equations and calculating change-of-variable in integration. Final recap: Matrix = Transformation, Determinant = Scaling Factor.
sections.example: Using a drone's perspective transformation matrix: if the determinant is zero, the drone's camera view has collapsed, indicating a loss of depth perception.

storyboard.title: Intuitive Hook: The Area Scaling Factor
lecture_lines: Linear transformations stretch the space around us.
Determinants measure the factor of area change.
A unit square transformed creates a parallelogram.
If area doubles, the determinant is two.
It quantifies how space scales during transformation.
animations: Animate transformation of square by 2x2 matrix.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The 2x2 Basic Calculation
lecture_lines: Determinants for two by two matrices use ad-bc.
Cross multiply vectors to find the area change.
Example: a matrix with result six scales area.
animations: Display 2x2 matrix A with elements in #00FFFF.
Animate calculation steps by highlighting a, d, b, c.

storyboard.title: Geometric Signification: Orientation and Zero
lecture_lines: Negative determinants indicate a mirror-image flip.
A zero determinant collapses shapes into lines.
Zero means the transformation loses a dimension.
animations: Show flipping orientation via reflection animation.
Demonstrate area shrinking to zero with collinear vectors.

storyboard.title: Scaling to 3D: Volume Interpretation
lecture_lines: Extend the concept to three dimensions now.
Determinants represent the volume scaling factor.
Transformations shrink or expand volumes in space.
animations: Animate transformation of cube by 3x3 matrix.

storyboard.title: Application and Summary
lecture_lines: Determinants solve systems and simplify integration.
Matrices represent transformations, determinants the scaling.
These tools are fundamental in applied mathematics.
animations: Summarize Determinant as scaling factor in #FFFFFF.
Fade out elements with a final text: 'Determinant'.
